doc: Application name must be topological_offset.
Tetrahedral input mesh.
Output file name (without extension).
Directory where the input files are located. This is injected by the application and should not be set by the user.
Boolean expression for input simplicial complex to offset. If a single tag (ie 'tag_0') is given, single body mode is used.
Tags to add to elements in the resulting offset region.
A tag.
Set of tags that will not be overwritten by the offset.
A tag.
Only relevant for single body mode. Whether to create offset inside body
Only relevant for single body mode. Whether to create offset outside body
Target offset distance relative to bounding box of mesh.
Target distance for offset. If < 0, the relative target distance is used to compute this one.

If true, a run that finishes without meeting the convergence criteria raises an error instead of logging a warning. Default false: a non-converged offset is still a usable one, and the warnings already name which criterion failed. Set true in integration tests so a convergence regression fails the run rather than passing with a warning nobody reads.

Half-width, relative to the bounding box diagonal, of the envelope containing every tag-region boundary during optimization. Any operation that would push a region boundary outside it is rejected. Ignored if envelope_size >= 0.
Absolute half-width of the tag-region boundary envelope. If < 0, computed from envelope_size_rel.

WHICH FIELD DEFINES THE OFFSET, and therefore what the boundary is placed on, what the criterion measures and what the sizing field refines by. `smooth` is the offset geometric contact potential Phi, with the boundary on the level set Phi = c: C^2, analytic derivatives, and a level set that BULGES OUTWARD at reentrant features, so it is a smoothed offset rather than the exact one. `euclidean` is the Euclidean distance d to the input complex, with the boundary on d = target_distance: the exact offset, with exact derivatives inside each closest-feature region, a gradient discontinuity across the medial axis, and a genuine crease at every reentrant feature that no refinement resolves. Two consequences of picking `euclidean`: the residual becomes EXACT (|d - delta|, with none of the reference-slope conversion the smooth field needs, which overstates wherever Phi's isolines are packed tighter than on a flat stretch), and offset_dhat_factor together with the outside-the-support guard become meaningless, because d has no compact support. `smooth` is the default and is what every measurement in this component was tuned against.

Support radius of the smooth offset potential, as a multiple of target_distance. Must be > 1. The offset level set lies strictly inside the support; a band vertex that leaves the support is a hard error.

THE CONVERGENCE TOLERANCE of the vertex test (Phase B pass stop and the A/B loop's vertex half); what it is a fraction OF depends on front_conv_criterion (see there). Default 0.001. It does NOT set the resolution: the edge test compares the level set's sagitta with offset_envelope_rel x target_distance (under gradient_norm_rel it still uses rel x the reference). Keep it small; a per-vertex, per-sweep tolerance cannot tell a slowly travelling front from a converged one, and 0.1 exited two_circles at 0.4 with the front at 0.22. ORIGINAL 2D DOC (gradient_norm_rel): THE CONVERGENCE CRITERION, as a fraction of a MEASURED maximum. 2D: the reference is max |2 (Phi - c) grad Phi . n| over the INITIAL offset-surface vertices -- n the surface's own Voronoi-length-weighted normal (offset_surface_normal) -- measured once on the band as constructed and reported as the log's gradient reference. The run converges when max ||2 (Phi - c) grad Phi|| over the reachable offset vertices falls to this fraction of that reference, and each Phase B per-vertex placement solve terminates on exactly the same comparison at its own vertex -- the overall and local criteria are IDENTICAL, so the run is converged precisely when every visit stops immediately. Edge-interior samples (offset_residual_samples per edge) are still measured as a chord diagnostic (max_grad_in_edge in the report) but do not gate: a sample is not a variable, and refinement rather than placement is what lowers it. So 0.1 means 'reduce every vertex's placement gradient to a tenth of the worst initial normal-aligned misplacement'. 3D: UNCHANGED and NOT the same meaning -- there the bound is still the analytic front_conv_rel x target_distance x level_set_slope()^2 on the full gradient norm, measured at vertices AND at in-face samples, both gating. The two dimensions share this key and interpret it differently; 3D was left alone deliberately.

2D. WHAT 'converged' MEANS for a front vertex, in Phase B's pass stop and in the A/B loop's vertex test, against front_conv_rel. THE SINGLE PHASE'S LOOP TEST (2026-08-29) is this vertex test AND nothing left to refine: a front edge whose two ends are within the tube of the level set (offset_envelope_rel x target_distance) and whose chord sags over the tube is refined by the resolution rule (target 3/4 L sqrt(tube/sag), the construction rule with the curvature read off the mesh; ends already at the sizing floor are reported, not looped on), and the loop exits only when no such edge is left. The four states placed / pressed / travelling / stuck are logged every turn for information (see offset_envelope_rel); gating on them was measured and rejected (pressed seams are stationary off the level set by definition). There is no other loop criterion (the old convergence_criterion key with 'gradient' and 'dist_and_orient' is gone, dist_and_orient is still logged for information). F is the vertex's Phase B objective (AMIPS + offset term + alignment term), g its gradient, H its (Gauss-Newton) Hessian; under front_normal_projection both are taken along the vertex normal n. 'gradient_norm_rel': |n . g| <= rel x reference, the reference being the same max on the band as constructed, measured once. 'step_size_rel' (default): the remaining 1-D Newton step |n . g| / (n^T H n) <= rel x target_distance -- no vertex would still move more than that fraction of the offset distance. 'decrement': the Newton decrement, half of (n . g)^2 / (n^T H n) = the energy the next Newton step would still gain, <= rel x F(x). WHY NOT THE GRADIENT (Uday, 2026-08-25): the gradient is stiffness x remaining displacement. Where two fronts meet, the strip between them is a sliver at the energy's minimum (AMIPS ~50), so a vertex 0.0001 x target_distance from its minimum still reads 13-19x the bar (Euclidean 0.4, rounds 2-4, the mesh visibly converged); the step and the decrement divide the stiffness out. THE EDGE TEST, same under all three: the second difference of (Phi - c)/c along every live front edge, |r(m) - (r(a) + r(b))/2| -- how far the level set curves away from the chord, which halving the edge reduces -- in gradient units against the reference under 'gradient_norm_rel'; under the other two as sagitta <= offset_envelope_rel x target_distance -- the level set resolved to within the tube Phase A already allows the front, so rel governs convergence only and never the mesh size (rel 0.01 with the edge test tied to it over-refined 0.04 to 5906 vertices for 1351). HISTORY: until 2026-08-26 a sizing rule halved an edge whose endpoints passed the vertex test and which failed this edge test; it fired at every crease every round and was removed. The 2026-08-29 resolution rule differs in three ways: an endpoint qualifies by being ON the level set (within the tube), not by having stopped moving, so a pressed seam never fires; the target comes from the measured sag (3/4 L sqrt(tube/sag), capped at 0.625 L so the split's children stay out of the collapse band) instead of halving; and an edge whose ends are already at the sizing floor is reported as unresolvable rather than refined again.

Sampling density used to measure the offset's residual BETWEEN its vertices. In 2D, k points in the interior of each band edge at i/(k+1), so k = 1 is the midpoint; in 3D, the interior lattice points of each offset-surface triangle at denominator k+2, so k = 1 is the centroid and the counts are 1, 3, 6, 10 for k = 1..4. 0 measures only at vertices, which is blind to a surface whose vertices sit on the level set while the elements between them cut across it.
Execute marching tets in decreasing order of edge length. Increases run time, may increase output mesh quality.
After performing offset, check if offset region is manifold
Save .vtu of output mesh

Samples per side of the grid the smooth offset potential is written on, as <output>_phi.vtu, for the viewer. 0 disables it. In 2D the grid covers the whole domain; in 3D a volume is unaffordable, so it is the PLANE through the box centre normal to the box's shortest extent. Carries phi, phi_residual_length and euclidean_distance per vertex; warp by phi to see the field as a height surface.

Write debug VTU frames of the evolving mesh. 2D (since 2026-08-26): one frame after every operation pass and every smoothing pass, as sequential files <output>_NNNNN.vtu so ParaView loads them as one time series, plus <output>_frames.txt with one 'NNNNN<tab>r<turn><phase><pass>_<op>' line per frame, which visualize_offset.py reads for its labels. 3D: only the per-phase timeline, one frame after every phase A and every phase B (<output>_phase_{round}{A|B}.vtu); see DEBUG_output_per_pass for the full per-pass series.

Also write a debug VTU frame after EVERY pass, not just the per-phase timeline: every phase A local-operations pass and every phase B smoothing pass, as <output>_debug_{N}.vtu on one shared counter so the two interleave in run order. Large -- measured on prism, 801 frames and 3.95 GB for phase A alone, and the two_spheres pinch ran 193 phase B passes on top of that. Observational: the frames do not consolidate and cannot change the run.
Logs are not just printed on the terminal but also saved in this file.
A JSON file that stores information about the result and the method execution, e.g., runtime.

Mesh storage (connectivity + attributes) is preallocated to this factor times the live element count at init and consolidation. Operations take fresh slots from that headroom and are retried once it is exhausted. Lower it for pure-decimation runs, raise it for aggressive refinement. The offset refines aggressively -- its surface has to reach the offset's own scale, not the background's -- so a run whose log carries [slots] warnings is dropping the very splits the criterion asked for.
Number of threads used for parallel execution (smoothing, edge collapse). 0 means single-threaded.

Smoothing passes after the ONE combined split+collapse+swap round of the shared optimization loop when interleaved_smoothing is OFF. Not read otherwise: with interleaving on (the default) the count is interleaved_smoothing_passes, everywhere. TriWild's key and TriWild's default.

Target edge length relative to the bounding box diagonal. Used to bound which edges edge collapse is allowed to touch (only edges shorter than 4/5 of this length are collapsed). Ignored if length >= 0.
Target edge length (absolute). If < 0, computed from length_rel.

Target AMIPS quality for tets. Default 100, matching the tetwild component -- Phase A is TetWild and stops where TetWild stops. Measured on prism: 100 converges in minutes; 10 pushes Phase A past what its operation set can deliver and the split pass becomes an unbounded refiner. Edge collapse will not push an already-on-target region's quality back above this.

3D only, DIAGNOSTIC. Refuse every edge collapse from the second A/B round onwards. The offset band is in a one-for-one stalemate on topological_offset_3d_convex -- 3010 splits produced an on-offset vertex and 3063 collapses removed one, net -53 over six rounds -- so the band cannot be refined however much the sizing field is lowered. This switches the collapse half off to establish whether the stalemate is what holds the residual up, at the cost of every guarantee coarsening provides. Not a fix and not for production use.

THE SHARED TRIWILD/TETWILD LOOP'S CAP, wherever that loop runs (one key since 2026-08-28; it was ab_phase_a_iterations, and an earlier max_iterations that nothing read): the pre-optimisation pass over the input (pre_optimize_input), Phase A of the alternating loop, and the finishing pass that runs with the front frozen after the single phase has placed it. The loop exits as soon as max AMIPS is under stop_energy, so this is an upper bound. Where the loop is REQUIRED to reach stop_energy (Phase A, the finishing pass) not reaching it within this many iterations is an error rather than a warning, because placing the offset on a mesh the improvement pass gave up on is not a result. TriWild's name and default.

Cap on Phase B's smoothing passes per round; negative (the default) means UNCAPPED. Phase B now runs passes until one completes with NO offset vertex backtracked by its one-ring (every local minimum interior), which is its natural fixed point: the potential is a frozen field, so offset placements couple only through the ring constraint, and the interior AMIPS solves that run in the same passes are what open those rings. A no-progress guard stops the phase with a warning if neither the constrained count nor the placement gradient improves over 10 consecutive passes; the run's own convergence bar (front_conv_rel) also ends the phase early. Set a positive cap only as a diagnostic override. HISTORY: the previous default of 2 was the mitigation for the Phase A dead-band ratchet seeded by the OLD placement-only B's front-loaded displacement (5/5 vs 3/5 on prism raw-construction, 2026-08-20); that B moved only offset vertices and relied on Phase A to repair the background, which is the design this replaces. NOTE: the 2D pipeline reads this cap too (negative = uncapped there as well, exiting on its displacement test).

2D, alternating loop only (unused when alternating_opt is false). Phase B's GAUSS-SEIDEL pass budget; the convergence criterion is the stop, this is the guard (Euclidean 0.2 on two_circles needs ~30 passes at front_conv_rel 0.01, and 20 cut every round short). Each pass gives every eligible vertex exactly ONE local iteration -- an offset-surface vertex takes one descent step on AMIPS + the offset error term, a background vertex one Newton step on its one-ring AMIPS -- sweeping in place so later vertices see earlier updates. The phase exits early ONLY on the run's own convergence criterion (the max placement gradient over offset vertices, front_conv_rel), otherwise it runs exactly this many passes. WHY: solving each vertex to its own minimum let a vertex race to a fixed point its neighbours had not yet seen, and where two offset fronts approach the same curve that crushed the elements between them into exactly-collinear zero-area triangles which no split or collapse can repair (measured on two_circles at delta 0.1). One step at a time advances the fronts together. The placement step is a damped Newton step with an Armijo line search, so its length comes from the local model rather than a constant; the pass count is therefore the only budget, and a vertex can cover real distance in one pass when the model says so.

3D only. Phase B stops when the largest vertex displacement in a pass falls below this fraction of the target edge length l. Relative rather than absolute so the test means the same thing at any model scale.

Phase B's per-vertex solve tolerance for the INTERIOR (background AMIPS) Newton solves, in both dimensions: each visit stops when the local energy gradient falls below this fraction of its own value at the visit's start (polysolve rel_grad_norm_tol). The 2D OFFSET placement does NOT read it: its gradient descent stops when the normal placement gradient |2(Phi-c) grad Phi . n| is at or under the run's own convergence bar (front_conv_rel x the measured reference), so one parameter governs the local offset solves and the global criterion alike. An entry-relative rule there had no absolute floor and limit-cycled: a vertex far inside the run's bar still owed a further 100x reduction it could not resolve at the fixed step size, and burned its whole iteration budget standing still. 3D still uses this key for BOTH of its Phase B solves (offset LM placement and interior AMIPS); see .claude/CLAUDE.md for the 3D edit that would close the gap.

THE ONE TOLERANCE OF THE 2D SINGLE PHASE (2026-08-28): a front vertex is placed when it is within eps x target_distance of its level set, a chord between two placed vertices is resolved when it sags less than that, and the loop exits when every front vertex is placed or pressed (stopped against another front, the input or a region boundary), none is travelling or stuck, and no chord is left to resolve; the resolution rule refines such chords with 3/4 L sqrt(eps delta / sag), the construction rule with the curvature read off the mesh. Also the half-width of the offset tube, AS A FRACTION OF target_distance -- the corridor the operations must keep the front inside (held while Phase A runs, rebuilt after every smoothing pass in the single-phase mode), and the tolerance the front's resolution is derived from at construction (L = 3/4 sqrt(8 eps delta rho)). 2D: eps = offset_envelope_rel * target_distance, a pure percentage -- the default 0.025 holds the offset boundary to within 2.5% of the offset distance while Phase A (TriWild: split, collapse, swap, smooth) runs, so at target_distance 1 the tube is 0.025 wide. Tighter over-constrains Phase A and starts refusing operations that were not straddling the boundary at all; looser lets Phase A undo placement Phase B had already brought inside tolerance. It is independent of the convergence criterion: that says when the run is done, this says how far Phase A may move the boundary while getting there. It was previously offset_envelope_rel * offset_residual_tolerance() with a default of 0.25, which came to the same 0.025 * target_distance at the default front_conv_rel of 0.2 -- but chained the tube to the criterion, and so, once the criterion became a fraction of a MEASURED reference, to how badly construction happened to place the band. 3D: STILL the old form, offset_envelope_rel * offset_residual_tolerance() (TopoOffsetTetMesh.cpp), so the new default makes the 3D tube 10x tighter than it was. 3D was left alone deliberately; see the note in .claude/CLAUDE.md.
Run split, collapse and swap as three separate rounds with smoothing after each, instead of one combined round. TriWild's default.

Smoothing passes after EACH operation group (split, collapse, swap) when interleaved_smoothing is on -- in the shared TriWild/TetWild loop (the pre-optimisation pass, Phase A, the frozen-front finishing pass) and in the 2D single-phase loop, which since 2026-08-28 reads this key too: it used to read num_smoothing_passes (2) while the passes around it read this one (1), so no single key set the smoothing count. Default 2 here (the shared engine's own is 1): each smoothing pass is one placement sweep of the front, and with one pass per group the front contracts half as fast -- measured 2026-08-28 on two_circles Euclidean 0.4: 11 turns at 1 against 5 at 2, same final result; 3 and 5 gain little more.

Run the post-optimization coarsening pass, as TriWild and TetWild do. It trades elements for nothing but the guarantee that the result is still good, so topological_offset holds it to an ABSOLUTE bar -- both AMIPS and the offset residual must be inside tolerance after each collapse -- rather than the non-degrading bar the main loop uses. OFF by default, matching wmtk::OptimizerParameters: the pass was measured at 86-96% of total runtime across seven tetwild models, and for the offset it is the last thing to run before Phase A checks its own convergence, so anything it degrades is reported as a Phase A failure rather than as a coarsening one. Turn it on per model when the element count is worth the time.

Coarsen as far as the quality guarantee allows, instead of stopping at the target edge length. The pass answers 'how few elements can hold this max energy', and that is a more aggressive question than it sounds -- the answer ignores how big the elements become. Measured on the registered tetwild models it takes them from 348k to 60k cells (-82.7%) at max energy raised on none of them, against -43.2% with this off, because a converged mesh is sized by length_rel and the adaptive sizing field rather than by what the quality target strictly requires. On by default: the element count is the thing worth having. Turned off, the pass leaves alone any edge already at or past the collapse threshold (0.8 * the target length, the same one the ordinary collapse uses), since collapsing it only makes its neighbours longer still. The sizing FIELD is deliberately not applied either way: that is the optimizer's own refinement scratch work, and honouring it here would leave the pass unable to undo refinement that turned out to be unnecessary.

Cap on the coarsen/smooth alternation; the pass also stops as soon as a round accepts no collapse. A round does NOT exist to finish what the previous one started: within a round the collapse pass already runs to a fixed point, so repeating the collapse alone finds nothing. What a round adds is the global smoothing in between, which moves that fixed point -- the dirty-epoch retry only re-offers failures next to a SUCCESSFUL collapse, so a whole-mesh smoothing pass is invisible to it, and a rejected composite is rolled back in full so rejections never accumulate progress within a round. Returns decay fast: measured over the 16 challenging triwild models at five rounds, accepted collapses by round were 68.8% / 21.7% / 7.2% / 1.8% / 0.5%. Every round costs a full pre-check sweep over all edges plus a smoothing pass, so the default is two -- they carry 90.5% of the coarsening, and the three that would follow are worth 9.5% for 60% of the pass's budget.
Ordinary whole-mesh smoothing passes run between coarsening rounds. This is what makes a second round worth running at all -- see coarsen_max_rounds -- so setting it to 0 collapses the rounds to one.

How far the local smoothing after each coarsening collapse reaches, in rings; the pass locks one ring wider than this. 1 rather than TriWild's and TetWild's 2, and the divergence is measured: a smaller ball perturbs less per collapse, so more of them clear the offset's absolute coarsening bar. On topological_offset_2d_dragon, 4210 collapses against 3664, 1092 more faces removed, a final metric of 0.849 against 0.896, and 15% less time.

Smoothing sweeps over the ring inside each candidate coarsening collapse, before its max energy is measured. This is what gives the collapse a chance to be judged on a relaxed neighbourhood rather than on the configuration it lands in. 0 by default, matching wmtk::OptimizerParameters: measured upstream, the ball averaged 98 vertices, so at two sweeps one candidate ran ~200 nonlinear solves and the pass ran 1.4 million of them to accept 5173 collapses -- and turning it off cost 0.2pp of cell reduction, inside the run-to-run spread, because the pass runs to a fixed point and finds another candidate instead. Note that with this at 0 the ONLY relaxation the pass does is the global smoothing between rounds, which has no per-operation accept test of its own -- see the forced quality veto in TetOptimizerMesh::coarsen_mesh().

Fire the sizing refinement when an iteration's improvement is small next to the distance the metric still has to cover: (prev - cur) <= stall_eps * (cur - target). 0 means only when it does not improve at all.

Iterations to skip after a sizing refinement before another may fire. Default 1, matching the tetwild component: the refined sizing needs one split/collapse round to act before the stall detector can fairly judge it. 0 allows one every iteration.
How many worst faces seed the refinement. 0 means every face above the filter threshold, which is TriWild's default.
Vertex rings grown around each seeded face before the sizing scalar is lowered.
Multiplicative reduction of the per-vertex sizing scalar per refinement.
Floor on the per-vertex sizing scalar.
Neighbouring sizing scalars may differ by at most this factor. The smoothing only ever lowers a scalar, spreading refinement outward. <= 1 disables it.
On a stall, also split each seeded face's longest edge once, bypassing the length gate and without touching the sizing field.

2D. Phase B places a front vertex by a ONE-DIMENSIONAL solve along its field normal n = grad Phi/|grad Phi|: the same objective (ring AMIPS + offset terms) restricted to the line x0 + s n, same solver, line search and accept test; the vertex test reads the step along the same n. Measured 2026-08-25 (two_circles, cap 20, rel 0.01): the free 2-D placement also converges everywhere under the step criterion, with 1-2 more rounds and more vertices, since the front slides tangentially while it travels. Until 2026-08-25 19:40 this was a stiff tangential penalty (k = 1e6) in the energy; it is not any more. ORIGINAL DOC: Phase B places a front vertex along the field's normal only (the direction of grad Phi at the visit's start), instead of the free 2-D solve. Where a vertex sits along the front carries no information about the offset; the 2-D solve's tangential motion is driven by AMIPS alone and made fronts slide and fold where two of them meet (measured 2026-08-25). Imposed as a stiff quadratic penalty on tangential displacement inside the front's own energy, so the shared smoother is unchanged; the pass stop and the loop's vertex test then measure |grad F . n|. Spacing along the front is left to Phase A's smoother.

2D. Whether Phase B's front objective carries the ALIGNMENT term, sum over the vertex's live front edges of (1 - n_e . ghat(m_e))^2 with n_e the edge normal and ghat the field's unit gradient at the edge midpoint, weighted like the offset term. It is what acts on the edge normals under front_normal_projection; measured 2026-08-25 on two_circles without it the worst seam edge angle against the field went 6 -> 17 deg at 0.10, 16 -> 26 at 0.15, 21 -> 39 at 0.20, for 10-15% fewer passes. ON BY DEFAULT, with a known cost (2026-08-29). Under the normal-only placement the term can only act along the normal, so it BIASES a vertex off its level set: measured 3-9% of target_distance on curved fronts, a sawtooth on the open half circle, and the annots staircase stuck at a Euclidean corner for 40 turns (a profile of the objective there shows the term jumping 0.16 -> 2.8 either side of the medial axis of the corner, where the Euclidean gradient flips: a cliff, not a minimum). What it buys is the pressed seam: with it the seam vertices reach the objective's stationary point in 4 turns on two_circles Euclidean 0.4 with a straight seam (spread 0.003); without it 14-23 turns at 0.4-0.5 and a rougher seam. Off for inputs with corners under the Euclidean field; the smooth field has no corners and no cliff. A corner-safe replacement is open.

2D. What the surviving vertex of a collapse keeps as its sizing scalar. false (default): its OWN scalar, the behaviour of the shared engine until 2026-08-27. true: the SMALLER of the two, the shared engine's rule since upstream 52315d39e2 ('unify the sizing field after collapsing'), applied here by restoring the survivor's scalar after the base collapse when false. Measured 2026-08-28 on the report matrix, same code otherwise: the min rule carries 16-93% more vertices on every case (two_circles Euclidean 0.4: 2186 -> 3696, the slot fixture 13741 -> 16451, two_overlap 687 -> 1323) and lengthens the placement loop where the front travels (Euclidean 0.4 at stop_energy 100: 4 turns -> 6; the slot fixture 2 -> 3; two_circles smooth 0.1: 7 -> 9). The offset's sizing follows a moving front and has to relax behind it; a scalar that only ever falls cannot. TriWild's convergence argument wants a sizing field that only refines (Daniele), which is what true gives; false reproduces the 2026-08-26 results to the digit.

2D. false (the default since 2026-08-26): ONE phase -- TriWild's own loop, with the front vertices placed by the one-dimensional offset solve inside its smoothing passes and free of the offset tube while they move, so operations and placement interleave at the pass level; the tube is rebuilt after every smoothing pass (only smoothing moves the front, and an operation that would take a front edge out of the tube is refused). Its turn budget is max_rounds. true: the A/B loop -- a full TriWild pass (Phase A, the front held in its tube and smoothed by AMIPS alone) followed by up to ab_phase_b_iterations Gauss-Seidel sweeps that place the front (Phase B), repeated up to max_rounds times; this is what 3D always runs. Measured 2026-08-26 over 12 cases: single phase uses fewer vertices nearly everywhere (the slot fixture 13741 against 31103, an inward offset 52019 against 103168), is faster in wall-clock on all but the smallest case, and converges one case the alternating loop does not. Convergence is the same test in both: every front vertex's remaining Newton step at most front_conv_rel x target_distance. Quality is then brought to stop_energy by a final pass with the front FROZEN -- while the front is being placed its rings cannot be repaired, since front placement carries no quality veto.

THE OUTER LOOP'S BUDGET, in both modes and both dimensions (one key since 2026-08-28; it was single_max_turns and ab_max_rounds). 2D single phase (alternating_opt false): the number of TURNS, one turn being split | collapse | swap with smoothing after each, followed by the front test; the loop leaves as soon as that test passes. Alternating loop (alternating_opt true; 3D always): the number of A/B ROUNDS, one round being a full Phase A (the shared TriWild/TetWild loop with the front held in its tube) followed by a full Phase B (the placement sweeps). An upper bound, not a schedule: exhausting it is a warning, not an error, because a front that needs more turns is a legitimate outcome to inspect. Default 40: measured 2026-08-26, the single phase places the front in 1-10 turns on every converging case (25 on two_overlap), so 40 is roughly four times the observed need; the alternating loop used to default to 10, and 40 only lengthens runs that do not converge.

What sizing field pre_optimize_input runs against. false (default): seed target_distance / l on the INPUT-COMPLEX BOUNDARY -- an edge with exactly one incident label-1 face -- and grade outward, so the complex is resolved at the offset's own scale and the marching band comes out one delta-scale cell thick. true: seed every vertex from the mean of its own incident edge lengths instead, i.e. 'keep the resolution you have', with target_distance not entering the field at all. The second is the weaker request: it improves element quality without refining toward delta, so the constructed offset lands wherever the input mesh's own scale puts it and dhat is sized from that. Only read when pre_optimize_input is true.

Run TriWild over the INPUT mesh before the offset is constructed -- before the simplicial embedding and the marching -- with the same Phase A parameters (stop_energy, max_iterations) and held only by the per-tag region envelopes, which exist by then. The sizing field is seeded at target_distance / l on the INPUT-COMPLEX BOUNDARY only -- an edge with exactly one incident label-1 face -- and graded outward by gradation_smooth_sizing()'s ring BFS; the complex interior is reached only by that gradation, never seeded. Resolving the complex at the offset's own scale is what makes the marching band one delta-scale cell thick, which is what puts the constructed offset near delta and keeps dhat small. WHY: the marching places the offset on the background triangulation's own cell boundaries, so how far the constructed offset lands from the input complex is a property of the INPUT MESH, and dhat is then sized from that reach. A coarse cell touching the complex therefore inflates dhat, and a dhat several times target_distance merges the level sets of nearby features (measured on two_circles: at 14.76x delta the potential's level sets across a 0.2 gap merge entirely). 2D only. ON by default (2026-08-26): without it the band is one input cell thick at construction, and on topological_offset_2d (input cells of 2 delta) that closed the 2-delta-wide slot mouths before the first placement; with it the band starts at 0.125 delta and the fixture converges. Off restores the input mesh as the later stages see it.

l_min: the shortest edge the sizing field may ask for, in absolute units. If < 0, derived as min_edge_length_rel * target_distance -- tied to the offset distance rather than the bounding box, because the offset is what has to be resolved. This is a floor on REFINEMENT, so raising it makes the offset coarser (paper Fig. 18).

l_min as a multiple of target_distance, used when min_edge_length is negative. Negative (the default) derives it as the Phase A offset envelope epsilon, which is now just offset_envelope_rel -- TetWild's own floor (cap the sizing below by the envelope eps, Sec 3.2) stated in the offset's units: the offset boundary is only held to within eps, so edges shorter than eps cannot buy fidelity. A pure anti-runaway rail, far below the chord length any tolerance actually needs, unlike the previous fixed 0.5176 = 2*sin(15 deg) default, which encoded the deleted normal-deviation criterion's sigma_max = 15 deg and silently capped achievable tolerance at ~3.3%.
Lower bound for the per-vertex sizing field (see max_sizing_scalar). Refinement stops once a vertex's sizing scalar reaches this fraction of the base target length.

Upper bound for the per-vertex sizing field, a multiplier on the target edge length (splitting_l2/collapsing_l2) refined/coarsened once per optimize_offset() iteration based on the mean ratio metric of the offset triangulation (see sizing_mrm_threshold). 1.0 means never coarser than the base target length.

Mean ratio metric threshold used to update the sizing field once per optimize_offset() iteration: for each offset-surface vertex, the sizing scalar is halved (refine) if the worst incident offset triangle's mean ratio metric is below this, or multiplied by 1.5 (coarsen) if above.

Gradation cap for the sizing field: neighboring vertices' sizing scalars may differ by at most this factor. After each mean-ratio-metric refinement pass, the refined vertices' lower sizing scalar is propagated outward (monotone, only ever lowers a neighbor's scalar) so the mesh doesn't jump straight from fine to coarse. <= 1 disables gradation.

Incident-tet count above which a vertex in a split edge's link accepts only one valence-increasing split per pass, or 0 to disable. Spreads refinement instead of letting it pile onto one vertex (only used if optimize is true).

Bisections tried by the projected line search before it gives up on a vertex: the step along the Newton direction is halved this many times, each candidate projected onto the input, and the first that does not invert and lowers the worst incident element is taken.

After the projected line search gives up, revisit each candidate and bisect between the interpolated point and its projection this many times, taking the longest step toward the input that still does not invert and still lowers the worst element. Lets a vertex whose one-ring cannot tolerate a full projection still travel toward the input, instead of being refused every pass from the same place. 0 disables the pass.

Whether smoothing refuses a move that raises the worst incident element's quality. True is TriWild's, SimWild's and TetWild's behaviour (3D ignores this key and forces true), and since 2026-08-25 the default here too. It was OFF while the offset boundary was placed by the shared smoother -- an offset term inside Phase A's objective whose minimum can be most of target_distance away, so the veto froze the boundary (measured: 0 of 6117 offset-vertex moves accepted on the dragon over a whole run). That premise is gone: Phase B places the front with its own solver and Phase A moves it by AMIPS alone inside the offset envelope, so Phase A is TriWild and takes TriWild's veto. Measured on two_circles 0.02 / 0.04: no difference; the key stays for experiments.

How smoothing places a surface vertex. 'projected': smooth with AMIPS alone as if interior, then walk back toward the start projecting each candidate onto the input; accept the first projected candidate that does not invert and strictly lowers the worst incident element, else do not move. Lands exactly on the input; no weights. 'exact': minimize w_amips * AMIPS + (1-w_amips) * (d/eps)^2 with the true region-wise Hessian of the distance to the piecewise-linear input; sliding is free where the input is flat, held at corners, constrained along 3D edges and curve segments. Rests a w_amips-proportional distance off the input.
Relative weight of the AMIPS quality term against the envelope term during smoothing of non-offset-surface vertices. The envelope weight is derived as 1 - w_amips (only used if optimize is true).
Check after every operation pass that no tet is inverted and no tracked-surface triangle left its envelope. Slow; for debugging (only used if optimize is true).
